provider: Google Chat spaces as a quota-exempt attachment store (Chat API media.upload/media.download)

free_tier.stated: Google Chat messages and attachments are content that doesn't count toward storage.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: The upload guide also says some file types are not supported and cannot be uploaded.

retention.stated: Admin-controlled: a Vault retention rule for Chat can discard messages after a retention period of 1 to 36,500 days, or keep them indefinitely.
retention.notes: Chat auto-deletion for 1:1, group and space messages accepts 30 to 36500 days. Supported editions for auto-deletion: Frontline Plus; Business Plus; Enterprise Standard and Enterprise Plus; Education Standard and Education Plus; Enterprise Essentials and Enterprise Essentials Plus. Vault retention rules (1 to 36,500 days) are a separate control.

egress.terms: media.download is limited to 3,000 attachment reads per 60 seconds per project; it supports the Range header for partial downloads. The Chat API pages read state no per-GB egress price and no byte quota.

tooling: REST over HTTPS: media download is GET https://chat.googleapis.com/v1/media/{resourceName=**}; the upload guide calls media.upload, then creates a message that attaches the file. No rclone backend is named on the pages read.
chaining: Writes are bounded by 600 media.upload calls per 60 seconds per project. The limits page states no per-day request limit while the per-minute quotas are respected. Whether quotas multiply across projects is not stated on the pages read.
limits_note: 200 MB per file hard cap; some file types blocked; 600 media.upload/min/project and 3,000 media.download/min/project; requires a Google Workspace account + Cloud project + Chat API enabled (personal @gmail.com accounts are not a supported developer surface; Chat API auth doc requires Workspace). Chat API quotas are per-minute only. The docs state 'no limit to the number of requests you can make per day' if you stay under them.

identity_cost.detail: The upload guide's prerequisite is a Business or Enterprise Google Workspace account with access to Google Chat. Payment details were not seen; no sign-up was entered.

reliability_note: Messages/attachments live in a space. Deleting or archiving the space, or removing the app from it, can orphan the data; no documented retention guarantee. Blocked MIME types must be avoided.

extras.document_section: Google Drive and its service-account history
extras.verified_at_basis: checked against the live service on 2026-11-10
extras.quota_verbatim: Per-record unlimited: 200 MB per attachment, and Chat messages AND attachments explicitly do NOT count toward Google storage quota. 600 attachment uploads/min/project x 200 MB = ~120 GB/min theoretical ingest.
extras.limits_verbatim: 200 MB per file hard cap; some file types blocked; 600 media.upload/min/project and 3,000 media.download/min/project; requires a Google Workspace account + Cloud project + Chat API enabled (personal @gmail.com accounts are not a supported developer surface; Chat API auth doc requires Workspace). Chat API quotas are per-minute only — the docs state 'no limit to the number of requests you can make per day' if you stay under them.
extras.egress_verbatim: Not metered — downloaded through Chat API media.download (3,000 attachment reads/min/project), supports Range requests. No per-GB charge in the docs.
extras.chaining_verbatim: Unlimited messages x 200 MB per attachment. 20 attachments per interactive message on web, but the API path is per-media-upload, so the binding constraint is the 600 uploads/min/project rate, and projects are multiplicative (30-project default quota per user). Storage is free because Chat attachments are quota-exempt — this is the strongest multiplier in the Google stack.
extras.tooling_verbatim: Official Chat API with service-account (app) auth; media.upload for write, GET /v1/media/{name}?alt=media for read with Range. No dedicated rclone backend exists — this is a build-it-yourself REST store; google-api-* client libs cover both directions.
extras.agent_focus: Google ecosystem: Drive service accounts + shared drives, Colab, Firebase, GCS free tier, Photos. Service-account chain as reference case, quantified.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
